justifications.technical_accuracy: RF probability, SHAP range and n-gram values match the evidence, and hedging is mostly appropriate. Minor overreach: "common in compiler output", "CALL PUSH ... call-return-then-setup flow", and "indicates many small function calls" assume adjacency and context not supplied. "All 20 top n-grams push toward the malware/cryptojacking class" also relies on the configured target-class assumption.
justifications.coherence: Explanation, per-feature assessments, key indicators, tier and recommended action are consistent. They repeatedly say the evidence is suggestive but not conclusive, matching the low-confidence tier.
justifications.cybersecurity_relevance: Ties the rotate/XOR/ADC n-grams to hashing-style computation and flags generic alternatives and missing function-level context. Some per-feature discussion is generic, and there is little discussion of benign crypto or checksum code as an alternative.
justifications.actionable_utility: Recommends function-level disassembly of the rotate/XOR/ADC sequences, sandbox dynamic analysis for pool connectivity and CPU-intensive loops, and packing checks, all concrete and conditional. Checking packing based on CALL RET and POP PUSH is weakly justified, and quarantine is somewhat generic but proportionate.
